value: The instance wiring links every class-space verb that has no instance link yet, instead of only wiring devices whose instance bin does not exist at all -- and it wires the instance a spawn just created, not only instance 0.

value.what: cairn restart cycles the system -- its verb lands in cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin, the class bin this wiring skips forever. That build makes its own link by hand; this ticket is why it should not have had to.
the dispatcher resolves an instance address. That ticket teaches `cairn cc.1 restart` to RESOLVE; this one makes there be something at the other end.
lifted the wiring recipe whole out of bootstrap_first_run.sh so it would have one address and two callers. This ticket fixes the unit of work inside that one address.
cairn_wire_instances -- _cairn_wire_device (the directory early return), _cairn_wire_single (the per-file rule to copy), and the discovery loop that passes 0.
cmd_spawn -- knows the instance number it just chose and today leaves it unwired.

value.text: Found while building Akien's three restart names. MEASURED: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin contains one hand-placed file (a shim-printing script, 338 bytes, placed 2026-09-02), and cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin does not exist in class-space at all -- so the cairn device has never been wired by the recipe and never will be while the directory-level early return stands.

retired.because: Q#75 answered (Akien 2026-11-09, outline 5.4.3.3.1): "why the hell would it need a heartbeat?" -- no watch; the four-tooth proof is the whole guarantee

decision.text: THE WATCHME PROBE, ARMED BEFORE THE CROSSING: cairn/devices/cairn/probes/every_class_verb_has_an_instance_link.py, a module declaring a module-level `PROBE` that is a frozen cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe built with keyword arguments why, trigger, to, verb, channel, body, carry, enough -- the shape cairn/devices/cc/probes/is_the_memory_curve_recorded.py is in, and it berths with what it watches (the cairn device, whose wiring this is) rather than with the ticket. ITS COMPARISON IS THE WIRING'S OWN, two directory reads and nothing more: for each `<repo>/cairn/devices/<dev>/0/bin/<verb>` that is an executable file, is there a `<instance root>/<dev>/0/bin/<verb>` that resolves to it? A device bin that IS its class bin answers yes for every verb by construction (D2) and is not a finding. TRIGGER: true on a beat where at least one class verb has no resolving instance link. It rides the heartbeat the ground loop already runs -- NO poller, no new clock, and nothing pokes it. CARRY: the UNLINKED VERB AND ITS DEVICE, never a boolean -- {"ticket": owning_ticket("f0ffa0db0952"), "device": "<dev>", "verb": "<verb>", "class_path": "<abs>", "expected_link": "<abs>"} -- so the carry says WHAT was missed rather than that something was, which is this ticket's watchme `carrier` verbatim. Surfaced on the cairn device's pane, because an unreachable verb is a live trouble and not a log line. ENOUGH: THREE VERBS ADDED TO ALREADY-WIRED DEVICES AND REACHABLE WITHOUT A HAND -- the count is of verbs added, NOT of clean beats, because a quiet week proves nothing about a rule that only bites when someone adds a verb. The probe therefore keeps, in instance-space at instance_path("cairn", 0) / "probes" / "every_class_verb_has_an_instance_link.json", the set of (device, verb) pairs it has ever seen in class-space; a pair not in that set is a VERB ADDED, and it counts toward `enough` only if it already resolves on the beat it is first seen. The probe carries NO AUTHORITY: it deposits and pokes, and the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act (Law 6).
